daily.title: Importer Need Not Challenge Assessment For Refund After Anti-Dumping Duty Set At Nil: Bombay High Court
daily.summary: The Bombay High Court has held that an importer need not challenge the assessment of bills of entry to claim a refund of provisional anti-dumping duty when the final duty is determined as nil.“The... “The refund becomes automatic after the Second Notification is issued under Section 9A(1) of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, and the same was required to be processed since the Anti-Dumping Duty was finally determined as 'Nil'. There is no necessity for the Respondent to thereafter file an appeal against the assessment or reassessment,” a bench of Justice B.P. Colabawalla and Justice Farhan P. Dubash observed.

daily.title: Consequential Assessment Invalid Once Original Reassessment Is Quashed: ITAT Hyderabad
daily.summary: Hyderabad ITAT held that a consequential assessment and CIT(A) remand directions cannot survive once the original reassessment is quashed for lack of jurisdicti Can a fresh assessment made under a CIT(A) remand order survive when the Tribunal subsequently quashes the original reassessment for lack of jurisdiction? The Hyderabad ITAT answered this question in Sri Light Chit Fund P. Ltd. v. ITO, ITA No. 2581/HYD/2026 , decided on 20 November 2026 for AY 2018–19 . The Bench held that the remand direction and the assessment made to give effect to it fell with the original reassessment.

daily.title: ITAT Raipur: CIT(A) Must Verify Additional Evidence on Merits Before Granting Relief
daily.summary: ITAT Raipur sets aside relief based on unverified additional evidence and directs a fresh remand report and speaking order under Section 250. The report contained no findings on the documents themselves . The CIT(A) recognised that the report had failed to serve its purpose. The appellate order also recorded that the Assessing Officer had earlier challenged the grant of relief without a remand report. Even so, the CIT(A) proceeded to grant relief by order dated 7 August 2026 , without recording any specific inquiry or verification of the additional material. The Revenue appealed to the Tribunal.

daily.summary: Manufacturers seek zero basic customs duty to support downstream industry The association said the existing levy, which becomes an effective import duty of 8.25 per cent after including the social welfare surcharge, creates a structural cost disadvantage for downstream manufacturers. The sector includes a large number of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), for which raw material costs account for a substantial share of overall manufacturing expenses. Primary aluminium prices in India are influenced by international prices and import-parity considerations, making customs duty an important component of the domestic price benchmark.

daily.summary: The Rajasthan High Court has recently ruled that interest awarded on motor accident compensation under Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, from the filing of a claim petition until the award,... A Full Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay K. Agrawal and Justices Sameer Jain and Bhuwan Goya l held that the interest forms an integral and inseparable part of compensation for death or bodily injury. It is merely compensatory and cannot be treated as a separate income in the hands of claimants.

daily.title: ITAT Hyderabad: Pre-Amendment Section 14A Disallowance Cannot Exceed Exempt Income
daily.summary: ITAT Hyderabad caps Section 14A disallowance at Rs.56.79 lakh and holds that the Finance Act 2022 amendment cannot apply retrospectively to AY 2018-19. Can the Assessing Officer disallow ₹5.35 crore under Section 14A when the company earned only ₹56.79 lakh in exempt income ? In DCIT Vs My Home Constructions Private Limited, ITA No. 2352/HYD/2025 , decided on 20 November 2026 , the Hyderabad ITAT held that, under the law applicable to AY 2018–19 , the disallowance could not exceed the exempt income earned during the year.

GTRI urges CBIC to issue guidelines to resolve Scotch whisky classification issue
daily.summary: GTRI has urged CBIC to issue classification guidelines for bulk Scotch whisky imports, amid a customs dispute that could raise the basic duty on such shipments from 75% to 150% under the India-UK trade pact. The trade pact halved the duty on qualifying Scotch whisky imports from 150% to 75% from 15 July 2026, with a further reduction to 40% by the tenth year of the agreement. However, in November 2026, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) directed the Customs Department to treat certain bulk Scotch shipments as beverage-making preparations under HS code 21069051, which attracts a 150% duty.
